title: Dynamic hysteresis and spike-echo suppression for KEDA/HPA hybrid autoscaling
creator: Avery Chen
description: Summary: After a recent capacity event where short, high-amplitude traffic bursts caused repeated scale-ups followed by rapid scale-downs (and several cold-start spikes), we observed an oscillation pattern we are calling 'spike-echo'. The pattern is caused by misaligned signals between KEDA (stream-based scaler) and HPA (metrics-based) plus conservative probe cooldowns that allow transient request waves to trigger full replica provisioning. This ticket captures the post-incident follow-up: diagnosis, short-term mitigations, and a longer-term algorithmic change to avoid future false positives/negatives without increasing steady-state cost.
incident_summary: On 2026-03-07 14:18 UTC a set of promotional events produced a bursty request profile. KEDA reacted to instantaneous stream counts and triggered rapid pod scale-up. HPA, which uses a 1m CPU average, lagged and then experienced a transient CPU bump when new pods saturated network init paths, causing additional KEDA triggers. Result: three scale cycles over ~12 minutes with 30% of requests served by cold starts and increased tail latency. Impact: customer-facing latency spikes (p95 -> p99) across several routes and temporary increase in cost for affected clusters.

root_cause: The root cause is the lack of a coordinated damping/hysteresis layer between event-driven scalers (KEDA) and metric-driven autoscalers (HPA). KEDA reacts to instantaneous peaks in event counts and can cause fast upscales; HPA reacts slower and uses averages that can appear as secondary signals. Additionally, probe cooldowns and init-time resource contention amplified cold-start penalties, creating positive feedback where transient cold-starts produced CPU spikes which KEDA incorrectly interpreted as sustained demand.
mitigations_taken: Applied a short-term KEDA suppression window (30s) for the affected scaler to avoid immediate re-triggers
Increased the HPA target stabilization window temporarily to reduce chattiness during the incident
Enable a lightweight warmup pod pool (2 replicas) for the critical service as a short-term cold-start mitigation
Disabled aggressive probe evictions that were causing premature pod termination during scale-down testing
action_items: ENG-SIG: Implement a cross-scaler hysteresis layer that computes time-weighted scale signals and exposes an API to KEDA/HPA (owner: Riley Patel, due: 2026-03-27)
Create a percentiles-based smoothing algorithm for stream-triggered scalers (use p50/p90 windows) and add it as an optional KEDA extension (owner: Linh Tran, estimate: 3, due: 2026-03-20)
Prototype a 'shadow-scaler' that simulates composite scale decisions in the control plane for 2 weeks before rollout (owner: Marcus Green, due: 2026-03-17)
Add synthetic fuzzy-load tests to CI to exercise transient bursts and validate hysteresis heuristics (owner: SRE team, estimate: 2, due: 2026-03-24)
Instrument and dashboard new signals: scale_decision_latency, effective_replicas, queue_depth_95, cold_start_rate (owner: Observability team, due: 2026-03-18)
Run a canary deploy of hysteresis layer in 'us-west-2' with 10% traffic and a rollback playbook (owner: Riley Patel, due: 2026-03-29)
Follow-up postmortem writeup with customer outreach notes and cost impact summarization (owner: Avery Chen, due: 2026-03-16)
Document recommended KEDA config defaults for bursty streams in our runbook (owner: DevX, due: 2026-03-21)
decisions: Prioritize a control-plane hysteresis layer rather than changing individual scaler heuristics across all services to avoid config sprawl
Adopt percentile-based smoothing as the canonical approach for event-driven scalers; keep a short suppression window as secondary protection
Introduce 'bootstrap stabilization' for new replicas: new pods get a short 'grace CPU headroom' to avoid init-time saturation being interpreted as demand
Canary rollout only after shadow-scaler has validated behavior for 7 days in production traffic
